questions.title: What exactly does the $\hat{n}$ parameter do in LongRoPE's positional interpolation?
questions.question_body: I am reading the problem formulation in Section 3.1, specifically Equation 4. It defines a function $\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_{i}, \hat{n})$ that is equal to 1 if $n < \hat{n}$ and $1/\lambda_i$ otherwise. I'm confused about the intuition here. Does this mean that for the first $\hat{n}$ tokens, the model simply uses the original pre-trained RoPE embeddings without any modification, and only tokens beyond that threshold are 'compressed' or interpolated? If so, why does this help with long-context extension?

questions.title: Why does extending the context window to 2048k degrade performance on short sequences?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions in the 'Shorter context window recovery' section that extending the window to 2048k causes a performance drop for shorter contexts (like 4k) because the positions become 'particularly crowded'. I don't quite understand the geometry of this. If we are only processing 4k tokens, why does the fact that the model *can* handle 2048k tokens make those 4k tokens feel 'crowded' in the embedding space? Does the value of $\lambda_i$ change depending on the actual sequence length during inference?

questions.title: How does the monotonicity constraint $\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}$ relate to the NTK-aware interpolation?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.2, the authors introduce a constraint where $\lambda_i$ must be non-decreasing across RoPE dimensions ($i=0, \dots, 63$). They mention this is based on NTK theory, suggesting that lower dimensions (higher frequency) require less interpolation. I'm trying to understand the connection: does this mean that the 'optimal' solution the evolutionary search is looking for is essentially a modified version of the NTK curve, or is the monotonicity constraint just a heuristic to prune the search space?

questions.title: In the progressive extension strategy, why is a second search used instead of further fine-tuning?
questions.question_body: I'm confused about the transition from 256k to 2048k. The paper says they fine-tune the model to 256k, but then they use a 'secondary search' to reach 2048k without any further fine-tuning. If fine-tuning was necessary to move from 4k to 256k, why is it not necessary to move from 256k to 2048k? Is the non-uniform interpolation search powerful enough to maintain model coherence at 2 million tokens without updating the actual weights of the LLM?

questions.title: Does LongRoPE perform extrapolation or interpolation for the first $\hat{n}$ tokens?
questions.question_body: I'm a bit lost on the terminology. The paper says they 'retain the starting tokens without position interpolation'. In the context of RoPE, does 'no interpolation' ($\lambda=1$) imply that these tokens are being treated as extrapolated, or does it simply mean they are using the original indices as seen during the initial 4k pre-training? I'm trying to figure out if these initial tokens are still within the original distribution of the pre-trained model.
